title: Scene editor keeps showing unrelated scene from another tab behind current scene until clicking that tab
body: ### Tested versions - Reproducible in v4.6.stable.official [89cea1439] ### System information Godot v4.6.stable - Windows 11 (build 26200) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3070 (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.6636) - 12th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i9-12900K (24 threads) - 63.75 GiB memory ### Issue description So I remember opening that bug already around Godot 4.0 but I'm unable to find it. It was very rare and hard to reproduce so nobody could really confirm it nor fix it. The problem is, it came back in Godot 4.3.stable and then later in Godot 4.6 just today. I don't know the exact conditions, but when working with several scenes with opened tabs and switching between them frequently, at some point, one of the scenes will get "stuck" and will keep being displayed behind the current scene in the Scene editor view. The nodes are not present in the Scene tree and you cannot select the "ghost" elements so it's very disturbing. In Godot 4.3: In Godot 4.6: Note how the Scene tree is almost empty but you can see two unrelated colliders in Scene view Other scenes are affected too Until you open the tab for the scene containing the culprit (the two colliders): then it will properly be removed when changing scene tab again: I suspect that the code that swaps the scene with another one in Scene editor view "fails" to clean up the old one at some point, due to some operation. ### Steps to reproduce Unfortunately I don't have a 100% reproducible issue, but I'm still opening this issue before I forget, and also in case someone here remembers the old issue I opened, so could mark this one as duplicate (unless you think it's back in Godot 4.6 for a different reason, as a regression). Anyway, some things you can try to trigger this: - Swap scene tabs repeatedly - Reload Saved Scene - Custom tool scripts that change the Area2D scale on some dummy colliders - Make some changes and save ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) N/A (I wish)
